meta.title: Provider website architecture: one application, many domains

blocks.title: Provider website architecture: one application serving many domains
blocks.subtitle: The tenant is resolved from the Host header, so every domain shares one deployment.

blocks.title: What a provider website has to deliver
blocks.lede: A branded shell around parts RentRemote already owns, multiplied across tenants.

blocks.note: Separate hosting combines the cost of N environments with the blast radius of one.

items.text: One provider website, keyed by website_id and provider_id.
Host header looked up in a cached domains table.
One deployable, split internally by defined interfaces.
Blade server-side, held full-page in Redis and at the edge.
Why thousands of domains need no thousands of IPs.
Property and pricing data, consumed and never authored.

blocks.title: The provider website is never a second source of truth
blocks.text: The provider website consumes RentOS data. It is never a second source of truth.

blocks.title: How responsibilities divide across the three layers

steps.title: DNS to shared edge

steps.title: Edge cache check
steps.text: A hit returns HTML without touching the app.

steps.title: TLS termination
steps.text: Wildcard or per-domain certificate, Host header intact.

steps.title: ResolveTenant middleware
steps.text: Host to website_id, cached in Redis.

steps.title: TenantContext bound
steps.text: Every later query is scoped, never client-supplied.

steps.title: Live call for the real-time slice
steps.text: Availability and payment bypass cache entirely.

blocks.note: A miss at step four is a controlled 404, never a fallthrough to a default tenant.

blocks.subtitle: Fifteen criteria scored 1 to 5 each. Judgement, not measurement.
blocks.note: The ranking is only as good as the criteria weighting, which is uniform here.

blocks.title: Method
items: Scores are judgement, 1-5 per criterion across 15 criteria, uniform weighting. They rank options against each other and are not a measurement of any deployed system.
Traffic split at the edge (80% cache hit) is a design target for the full-page cache, not an observed figure.
Tenant scale of 500+ sites is the planning target agreed for the first two years.
